featured.name: AegisScan
featured.tagline: All in one AI correlated cybersecurity scanner
featured.summary: A multi layer security scanner covering web apps, APIs, networks and configurations, fused with intelligent AI correlation so signal beats noise.
longSummary: AegisScan is the tool I wish I had when I first started running pentests. Most teams stitch together five separate scanners and then spend the first hour of every engagement copy pasting findings between tabs. AegisScan runs all of them in a single pass and lets a language model do the boring correlation work.

The flagship feature is the correlation engine. When a port scan, a configuration audit, and a web application scanner all flag the same host, AegisScan clusters them into a single attack story with severity, evidence, and a remediation hint. Analysts triage one ranked feed instead of five disjoint reports.
It was built to be useful in both modes a working SOC actually needs. Quick external assessment for a new client, and deep recurring audit for an existing one.
featured.problem: Security teams drown in scanner output. Five tools produce five disjoint reports, and the actual exploit chain hides between them. Triaging that manually wastes the first hour of every incident.
featured.approach: AegisScan runs web, API, network, and configuration scanners in one pass, then pipes their findings into an LLM backed correlation layer that clusters related signals into a single attack story. Each finding lands with severity, evidence, and a remediation hint.

featured.name: Real Time Threat Detection
featured.tagline: ML driven multi cloud SOC pipeline
featured.summary: A production grade detection system that streams events from AWS and Azure into ML models to flag threats in real time across both clouds.
longSummary: When I dug into how most SOCs handle multi cloud, the answer was depressing. Two tabs. AWS in one, Azure in the other. Attackers laugh at that boundary because they pivot across it. This project was about deleting that boundary.

It ingests CloudTrail and Azure Monitor events, runs them through a feature pipeline I built for security telemetry, then scores each event with a hybrid anomaly plus classification model. Both clouds land in one queue with one consistent severity scale.

I treated SOC analyst experience as the design constraint. The model output had to be one ranked queue, not two. Each alert had to include the raw event, the model confidence, and the source cloud, so an analyst could pivot in seconds.
featured.problem: Most SOC tooling treats AWS and Azure as separate worlds. Attackers don't. They pivot. We needed a single pipeline that ingested both clouds and learned what normal looks like.
featured.approach: Built a streaming ingest from CloudTrail and Azure Monitor into a feature pipeline, trained anomaly and classification models on labelled events, and exposed alerts through a unified API so SOC analysts see one queue, not two.

featured.name: AI Security Analyst
featured.tagline: Multi agent SOC assistant powered by Gemini
featured.duration: Solo build, in production at Securovix
featured.summary: A multi agent cybersecurity system that automates log analysis, anomaly detection, threat intel lookup, response recommendations, and incident report generation.
longSummary: A junior SOC analyst spends most of their day on the boring 80%. Tail a log. Search for an indicator. Look up an IP on a threat intel provider. Write the same report for the fifth time today. The work scales linearly with alert volume and burnout follows close behind.

AI Security Analyst splits that workload across specialised agents. A log parser, an anomaly detector, a threat intel agent, a responder, and a reporter. Each one has a narrow scope and a small tool surface. An orchestrator decides which agent gets which sub task and how the output gets stitched back together.

FastAPI exposes the system as a real time API. A batch CLI runs the same pipeline over historical logs so analysts can re sweep past data with new context. The output is always an analyst ready report, never raw model text.

featured.name: Autonomus
featured.tagline: Detect, remediate and prove cloud compliance autonomously
featured.summary: A production grade platform that autonomously detects compliance drift across cloud environments, remediates it, and produces audit ready evidence.
longSummary: Most compliance programmes I have walked into ship spreadsheets. Engineering teams ship infrastructure. The gap between what the policy says and what the cloud actually looks like is exactly where audits fail and where attackers live.

Autonomus closes that gap continuously. It evaluates live cloud state against a policy as code rule set, classifies each drift by safe to fix versus needs human, executes the safe fixes itself, and records every action in an immutable audit log that satisfies the standard.

I built it to be useful to the compliance team and the engineering team at the same time. Compliance sees one dashboard that says current state is green. Engineering sees the same dashboard with the receipts of what was changed and why.

featured.approach: Continuously scans cloud accounts against policy as code rules, auto remediates safe deltas like open S3 buckets, dangling IAM, public security groups, and bundles every action into an immutable audit trail.

featured.name: Automated ETL for Financial Analytics
featured.tagline: Production ETL across fifteen plus financial data sources
featured.summary: A production ready ETL pipeline for financial analytics with fifteen plus data sources, automated validation, transformation, and orchestration.
longSummary: Finance teams ship under deadline. By month end the reporting tower of Excel macros, vendor exports and copy paste joins always cracks. I rebuilt that pipeline as something the team could trust on the worst day of the month.

Each of the fifteen plus sources is a plug in adapter with its own retry, auth, and rate limit story. Transforms are idempotent and tested. Loads are idempotent and safe to re run after a partial failure. Validation gates between every stage stop bad source data from poisoning downstream reports.
It cut reporting time from hours to minutes and lifted refresh reliability by 85%. More importantly the finance team stopped firefighting and started analysing.

featured.tagline: Seventy percent plus ticket auto resolution

featured.summary: Production ready IT support automation that auto resolves IT tickets with a 70% plus resolution rate.
longSummary: I spent a year as the IT support technician at SecureTech Insight. By the end of month two I could write the resolution to most tickets in my sleep. Password resets, mailbox permissions, VPN problems, printer drivers. Same flow every time.

So I automated it. The system classifies inbound tickets, matches them against a runbook library, and executes safe remediations directly against AD, O365 and the device management APIs. Tickets the system is not confident on get routed to a human, but with the diagnostic context already collected.
It hit 70% plus auto resolution. The non obvious win was on the remaining 30%. Those tickets land with the analyst already half done, because the diagnostics ran first.

featured.name: Network Intrusion Detection
featured.tagline: ML based intrusion detection on network flows
featured.summary: Machine learning network intrusion detection system trained on labelled flow data to spot intrusions in real traffic.
longSummary: Signature based IDS misses anything novel. Pure anomaly detection over fires. The trick is to learn what flow behaviour normally looks like and only alert when the deviation matters operationally.

I feature engineered network flow records, trained classifiers on labelled intrusion data, and tuned thresholds against false positive cost, not just precision. The model lives next to traditional signature engines, not instead of them.
The result is a hybrid detection layer that catches novel patterns the signatures miss without burying the analyst in noise.
